title: Reserve lease allocator and fallback negotiator — PRD (rough)
body:
Goal:
Create a lightweight reserve-lease allocator that lets tenants hold short-term compute leases (seconds->hours) with configurable fallback/eviction behavior and a mediated burst market so Dedicated pools can absorb transient demand without global overcommit. This doc describes product-level primitives, operator UI, SLO interactions, and a rough operator runbook.

Context / why this: (notes to self)
- Customers want predictable baseline capacity but also an escape hatch for unpredictable traffic (seasonal spikes, marketing bursts).
- Existing approaches (hard reserved, simple burst credits) either waste capacity or require manual ops.
- We can improve utilization by allowing controlled, priced bursts with well-defined fallback semantics to preserve SLOs for committed tenants.

Key primitives (first pass):
- Lease: short-duration reservation (min 30s, max configurable per pool). Leases consume a weighted slot count.
- Soft-lease: preemptible lease with cheaper unit price, 30s warning before eviction.
- Hard-lease: non-preemptible for committed capacity (maps to existing Reserved).
- Burst-credit: token bucket issued daily; credits can be spent to acquire soft-leases on-demand when pool capacity available.
- Fallback policy: per-tenant policy that defines where traffic routes on preemption: fallback model variant, degraded latency lane, or queued retry.

Autoscaling interaction:
- Leases can be autosized: tenant requests target qps/throughput, allocator translates to lease quantity based on historical p99 token rates.
- Autoscaler aligns physical GPU warm pools to expected lease demand. Negative feedback if preemption > X/sec triggers conservative scaling.

Economic / governance model:
- Pricing tiers: free burst credits (small monthly allotment), pay-per-burst credits, subscription for sustained burst capacity.
- Credit decay: unused credits expire monthly to prevent hoarding.
- Emergency override: SRE can mark pool as frozen (no soft-lease creation) during incidents.

Isolation / safety fences:
- Isolation curve: new allocator enforces tenant burst caps proportional to SLA weight.
- Noisy neighbor detection: if tenant uses >alpha of burst-credits continuously, move to soft-quarantine (reduced burst admission).
- Admission gate: estimator rejects soft-lease if projected p99 impact on committed tenants > allowed delta.

API surface (sketch):
- POST /v1/dedicated/leases {tenant_id, duration_secs, type: soft|hard, target_tokens, fallback_policy_id}
- GET /v1/dedicated/lease/{id} -> state, expires_at, preemption_eta
- PATCH /v1/dedicated/tenant/{id}/burst-policy -> caps, credit_balance

Operator UX / Console:
- Pool dashboard: active leases, headroom %, projected 1h demand, hot tenants list.
- Tenant view: current leases, credit balance, preemption history, recommended fallback mapping.

Monitoring / SLOs to track:
- Preemption rate (per tenant, per pool) — alert if > 0.5% of requests are preempted in 15m window
- Latency regression (committed tenants) after soft-lease admission — rollback/auto-throttle if p95 increases > 10%
- Credit spend velocity and predicted exhaustion window
- Pool headroom trend (5m, 1h, 24h)

Runbook highlights (operational notes):
- Detection: high preemptions -> check recent lease admission events and admission gate logs
- Mitigation: temporarily increase soft-lease price for offending tenant, or apply soft-quarantine
- Incident: if committed SLOs violated, freeze new soft-leases and spin up emergency warm-pool nodes (requires SRE approval)

Open questions / TODOs:
- How granular should leases be for multi-model serving (token-based vs slot-based)? (ACTION: engineering to prototype both by 2025-11-21)
- Does credit market need secondary trading between tenants (likely no for first iteration)?
- Backfill behavior for preempted in-flight requests — rely on client retry/backoff or server-side continuation?
- Exact pricing matrix (product + finance to propose).

Related references and signals:
- See CONFS-1729 for benchmarking of p99 impact when admitting soft-leases (Aisha).
- RFC: lease-metadata-and-telemetry (internal) — draft in GH gist (link in JIRA ticket).

Notes about implementation risk:
- Correct admission estimator is critical; conservative defaults required for MVP.
- Telemetry volume will increase (lease events + admission scoring) — need retention plan in Console.

Next steps (short timeline):
- Nov 10: engineering spike to simulate admission estimator and headroom model (Marco)
- Nov 21: propose pricing and credit policy (product + finance)
- Dec 05: internal alpha with 3 pilot tenants and observability hooks

Quick TODOs (for this doc):
- Add example UI mockups (Sophie)
- Draft API contract for review (Marco)
- Fill in exact alert thresholds and playbook steps (SRE)

---
Ravi (notes)
summary: Draft PRD for a reserve-lease allocator that supports soft/hard leases, burst credits, and mediated fallback policies to improve Dedicated pool utilization while protecting committed tenants. Includes API sketch, operator UX, monitoring and runbook notes.
